external_research.kanu: Kanu AI is an a16z speedrun company positioned as an 'AI Cloud Engineer' (getkanu.com). A web search did not surface its launch film, so NOTHING in this spec is derived from Kanu's film. Only the storytelling principles named in the brief are used (belief-first, short statements, minimal UI, gradual reveal, system diagrams, product evidence, whitespace).
external_research.remotion: Confirmed in Remotion docs: <CameraMotionBlur> (shutterAngle, samples), <Trail>, @remotion/transitions <TransitionSeries> with presentations including fade, slide, wipe and blur variants. Sources: remotion.dev/docs/motion-blur-guide, remotion.dev/docs/transitions.

constraints_honoured: No Navis-AI, Devtool, Backend or website source file was modified. This JSON is a new, untracked file beside navis_code_audit.json.
No status is upgraded beyond the evidence. Where this pass found the audit too generous, the status was downgraded (see contradictions_and_resolutions).
No metric, valuation or availability is asserted as fact.

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The audit lists real Gmail, Calendar AND Slack senders. Core has slack_sender wired, but there is no Slack install/connect route (grep of Backend routes on 2026-10-04 found only /integrations/slack/disconnect and /webhooks/slack/events). The 2026-09-25 market research says the same.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Slack is excluded from the film. An organization cannot connect Slack through the product, so showing Slack execution would imply a customer can do it.

contradictions_and_resolutions.topic: What the work-state checkpoint captures automatically
contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The audit's cinematic shot list implied decisions are captured automatically. hook.ts buildPatch (lines ~898-956) shows hooks infer only objective, current and open from prompts. Decisions and completed work are written only by `navis workstate checkpoint --decision/--completed`.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Day 1 shows the agent recording its decision with `navis workstate checkpoint` (instructed by a CLAUDE.md line in the demo repo). The VO says 'the decisions it recorded'. Automatic capture is listed in claims_to_avoid.

contradictions_and_resolutions.topic: Visibility of the restored block in Claude Code
contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: SessionStart stdout is injected into the MODEL's context. Whether the Claude Code UI shows it to the person (as opposed to the transcript view) is not proven by code in these repos.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: The on-camera proof is (1) Claude's first reply quoting the recorded decision and open item after the developer types only 'continue', plus (2) a macro of the block from Claude Code's transcript view if it renders there. Verify in rehearsal; if (2) is unavailable, S08 uses (1) alone.

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The audit cites ~3.4 s (uncommitted Core fixes, 2026-09-25); the market research cites 17-25 s; hook.ts comments cite 20.8 s on a cold local Core.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Latency is UNKNOWN on the filming environment. The film never claims speed; waits are shortened by cuts and disclosed in the end legal line ('Some waits shortened').

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The audit suggested 'real free slots -> approve -> invite appears'. The multi-turn scheduling path (POST /chat -> proposal -> ScheduleMeetingProposalCard -> calendar_sender) was not traced to its terminal UI state.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Downgraded to status unknown. It is an optional alternate (ALT_B), not in the master cut.

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The brief frames the shared layer as 'organizational intelligence'. The team's own 2026-09-25 market research advises against it as a headline noun (collision with people-analytics vendors, inconsistent use on navislabs.in), and against 'company brain' and 'memory'.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Recommended default: 'organizational intelligence' appears ONCE, in the closing line, as the category the whole film earns; every other line uses concrete nouns (decisions, what's open, who's waiting, sources, approval). Needs founder sign-off (U01).

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The brief names the people product 'NAVIS-AI'. Its UI brands itself 'Navis' (title 'Navis · Organizational Intelligence', masthead 'Today · Navis'); 'Navis-AI' is the repository name. The developer product is 'Navis Developer' in the console's page titles.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Default on-screen labels: 'NAVIS AI · FOR PEOPLE' and 'NAVIS DEVELOPER · FOR AGENTS' (brief's naming, hyphen dropped for typography). Needs founder sign-off (U02).

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The lifecycle UI is real, but real-world outcome capture is webhook-only and Learning does not read agent runs (research §25; Core record_outcome emits no event).
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: The lifecycle is not a hero beat. Outcome -> Learning appears only in the FUTURE loop (S16), drawn dashed and labelled NEXT.

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: Research §23 notes draft bodies can be boilerplate.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: S13 includes a real human edit on camera. The generated portion is never rewritten in post.

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: The 0/12 cross-org breach result is from 2026-09-28, not today.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Re-run the isolation check on the filming environment before shooting S10 (gate QG06).

contradictions_and_resolutions.conflict: navis-labs-website ships a hero film (vintage cartoon footage) and a music file (paper-kite-drift.mp3) of unknown licensing.
contradictions_and_resolutions.resolution: Neither is reused. Music is commissioned or licensed fresh with stems.

creative_direction.one_sentence: A quiet, belief-first film that proves, with real product footage, that Navis gives agents and people the same cited, permissioned understanding of a company, and leaves the viewer seeing Navis as the layer between companies, humans and AI agents.
creative_direction.viewer_takeaway: Navis is building the organizational intelligence layer between companies, humans and AI agents.

thesis_variations.text: AI knows the world. It doesn't know your company.
thesis_variations.notes: Plain, familiar nouns, instantly legible. Risk: Glean/Rovo occupy 'knows your company' (research §21), so differentiation must come from the proof beats.

thesis_variations.text: The model will change. The agent will change. What your company knows should persist.
thesis_variations.notes: The strategic thesis: Navis outlives model and agent churn. Best as the belief beat, not the hook.

thesis_variations.text: The smartest model in the world is new at your company. Every day.
thesis_variations.notes: Vivid and slightly witty. Strong for the aggressive VO.

thesis_variations.text: Your agents know the code. They don't know what your company decided.
thesis_variations.notes: Developer-precise (mirrors research direction #2). Too narrow for a two-product film.

thesis_variations.text: Stop re-briefing your agents. Stop leaving people waiting.
thesis_variations.notes: The research's 'follow-through' concept. Concrete, but two imperatives read like a feature list.

thesis_variations.text: Intelligence is everywhere. Context is local.
thesis_variations.notes: Elegant but abstract; 'context' is a saturated word.

thesis_variations.text: A company is the sum of what it has decided.
thesis_variations.notes: Philosophical; weak link to the product proof.

thesis_variations.text: One understanding of your company, for every person and every agent.
thesis_variations.notes: Good end line; descriptive rather than a hook.

selected_thesis.end_line: derived from T8 and the user's framing: 'Navis. Your company's intelligence — for your people, and your agents.'
selected_thesis.rationale: T1 creates the gap in two short sentences, T2 states the belief that justifies a company existing to close it, and the proof beats (continuity, cited context, isolation, approval) differentiate Navis from 'search over your docs'.

narrative_spine: AGENTS: it asks the company, with sources
AGENTS: each key sees only its own

visual_grammar.rule: DARK = AGENTS. LIGHT = PEOPLE. THE BLUE LINE = NAVIS.
visual_grammar.dark_world: Warm near-black #14130F, mono typography, terminal windows. Used for the opening gap and the Navis Developer act.
visual_grammar.light_world: Warm white #F7F6F3, the product's own light UI. Used for the Navis AI act.
visual_grammar.blue_line: A single 2 px line in logo blue #1976FE. It is born when fragments converge (S03->S05), becomes the horizon that wipes from the agent world to the people world (S11), the vertical seam between AGENTS and PEOPLE (S15), and bends into the loop (S16). It is the ONLY saturated color in the film outside product UI.
visual_grammar.why: The viewer learns the two products by world, not by reading labels, and the shared layer is literally the thing both worlds touch.

claims.text: AI knows the world. It doesn't know your company.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: A point of view, not a capability claim.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: No statistic or study is implied.

claims.text: …so every new session starts with a re-brief.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: Describes the felt problem documented in research; makes no number claim.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Do not say agents remember nothing — Claude Code re-injects CLAUDE.md and its own memory. Do not cite the 5.7k-character re-brief figure.

claims.text: For agents, Navis keeps the work state.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: The checkpoint is stored on the Core ledger as the run outcome and verified on read-back.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Not a transcript, not conversation memory, not model memory, not automatic capture of files or tests.

claims.text: Tomorrow, a fresh one opens with the objective, the decisions it recorded, and what's still open.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: SessionStart restores the stored checkpoint; the decision is shown being recorded on Day 1 (S07).
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Not 'everything from yesterday'; not other agents (Codex/Cursor); not teammates.

claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: Literally true in R03: the developer's only input is 'continue'.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: If the take needs any extra instruction, this line must change.

claims.text: When the task depends on your company, the agent asks Navis — and gets the facts that bear on it. With sources. With how fresh they are.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: The tool returns items with kind/source/lineage, plus freshness (as_of, newest_fact_at) and sources (auth_state, last_success_at).
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Not 'instant' or 'real-time'; not 'Navis AI writes the answer' (no generative model is called); not 'reads your documents' (Drive is metadata only).

claims.where: VO L14 + on-screen 'YOUR CONTEXT STAYS YOURS' / S10
claims.text: Every key sees only what it's allowed to — and only its own company.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: Shown with three real outputs (Org A, Org B, restricted key) recorded on the filming environment after QG06 passes.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: No absolute security guarantee ('never', 'impossible', 'certified'); no SOC 2; no mention of credential management (open Core P0).

claims.text: For people, the same understanding becomes your morning. Who's waiting on you. The reply, already drafted.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: Today surfaces waiting-reply obligations from real ingested mail; drafts come from the execution service.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Not 'in your voice', not perfect drafts, not 'every morning automatically' unless the brief schedule is verified.

claims.text: You read it. You approve it. Navis sends it — and only says sent when Gmail confirms.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: 'Reply sent' renders only when provider_reference holds a real external id; approval is the only path (no auto-execution).
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Not 'read-only', not 'autonomous', not Slack, not 'tracks whether they replied'. On-screen 'SENT' may appear only after the UI shows 'Reply sent'.

claims.where: VO L19 + on-screen 'ONE SHARED UNDERSTANDING' / S15
claims.text: People and agents, working from one shared understanding of your company.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: Both products read one Core implementation of the organization's context.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Not that an agent's coding work shows up in Navis AI; not team-shared work state; not Slack/Notion/CRM sources.

claims.text: Next: every outcome feeds back into what it knows.
claims.why_it_is_safe_to_show: Spoken and drawn explicitly as NEXT, after the present-tense proof.
claims.what_must_not_be_claimed: Never 'learns from every interaction' or 'self-improving' in the present tense.

lines.text: AI knows the world.
It doesn’t know your company.
What was decided. Who’s waiting. What’s still open.
It lives in inboxes, calendars and people’s heads — so every new session starts with a re-brief.
Models will change. Agents will change.
What your company knows should persist.
This is Navis.
For agents, Navis keeps the work state.
Close the session tonight.
Tomorrow, a fresh one opens with the objective, the decisions it recorded, and what’s still open.
You type one word.
When the task depends on your company, the agent asks Navis —
and gets the facts that bear on it. With sources. With how fresh they are.
Every key sees only what it’s allowed to — and only its own company.
For people, the same understanding becomes your morning.
Who’s waiting on you. The reply, already drafted.
You read it. You approve it.
Navis sends it — and only says sent when Gmail confirms.
People and agents, working from one shared understanding of your company.
Next: every outcome feeds back into what it knows.
Navis. Your company’s intelligence — for your people, and your agents.

aggressive.text: The smartest model in the world is new at your company. Every single day. It doesn’t know what you decided. Who’s waiting on you. What’s still open. That lives in inboxes, calendars and people’s heads. Models will keep changing. Agents will keep changing. What your company knows has to stay. This is Navis. For agents: close the session tonight. Tomorrow, the work state is back — the objective, the decisions it recorded, what’s still open. One word, and it continues. Ask your company from inside your agent, and get the facts that bear on the task — with sources, with how fresh they are. Every key sees only what it’s allowed to. Only its own company. For people: who’s waiting on you, and the reply, already drafted. You read it. You approve. Navis sends. And it says sent only when Gmail says so. One shared understanding, for your people and your agents. Next, every outcome teaches it. Navis. Your company’s intelligence. For your people. And your agents.
aggressive.risk: 'has to stay' and 'teaches it' push harder; 'Next' must stay audible.

understated.text: AI knows a great deal about the world, and very little about your company. The decisions that were made. The people who are waiting. The work that is still open. Most of it lives in inboxes, calendars and memory. Models will change, and so will agents. What your company knows should carry on. This is Navis. For agents, it keeps the state of the work. A new session begins with what was decided and what remains, so the work doesn’t have to be explained again. When a task touches your company, the agent can ask — and receives cited facts, with their age. Each key sees only its own company, and only what it is permitted to see. For people, the same understanding arrives as a morning: who is waiting, with a reply already drafted. You decide. Navis sends, and confirms only what Gmail confirms. One understanding, shared by people and agents. In time, every outcome will feed back into it. Navis.
understated.risk: Elegant but low energy for a launch; weaker end line.

rules: One statement on screen at a time.
Statements center-aligned; captions left-aligned to the 96 px safe margin.
No italics, no gradients on type, no outlines.

background_treatment.dark: Solid ink #14130F with a radial lift at (50%, 115%): rgba(25,118,254,0.08) -> transparent over 60% of height, present only after the blue line exists (S05 onward).
background_treatment.light: Canvas #F7F6F3 with a soft edge falloff to #EFECE6 (radial, 0.85 -> 1.0 radius).
background_treatment.grain: Monochrome film grain, 2.5% opacity on dark, 1.5% on light, 1:1 pixel, animated each frame (tiled 512 px noise texture offset per frame).

card_language.glass: rgba(255,255,255,0.72) + 24 px backdrop blur, only for floating labels over light UI

visual_system.glow: Only the Navis blue line: 2 px core #1976FE plus 0 0 24px rgba(25,118,254,0.45). Nothing else glows.

terminal.title: repository name only, e.g. 'fieldstone-api'
terminal.content: cropped recording of the terminal content area only (real chrome cropped out)

browser.address_bar: blank pill or the text 'Navis' — NEVER a URL (no localhost, no staging, no invented production domain)
browser.content: cropped recording of the page viewport only

window_chrome.window_placement: Default window box 1600x1000 world px centered; recordings are 2x (3200x2000) so camera zoom up to 2.0 stays sharp.

cursor.style: macOS arrow, black fill with 1.5 px white outline, rendered at 1.25x (32 px)
cursor.click_feedback: ring 20 -> 44 px, 1 px, ink 22% on light / white 25% on dark, 220 ms, settle easing; pointer scales 1 -> 0.92 -> 1 over 120 ms
cursor.hidden_in: terminal scenes (keyboard only; the real text caret is visible)

visual_system.spacing: 8 px base grid; caption-to-window gap 32 px; label tracking per hierarchy

motion_system.text_reveal: Opacity 0 -> 1, translateY 12 -> 0 px, blur 6 -> 0 px over 21 frames (settle). Exit: opacity 1 -> 0, blur 0 -> 4 px over 12 frames (exit). No typewriter effects; only real typing is ever seen typing.

camera_model.convention: Each scene has a world plane in px with origin at its center. camera.x/camera.y is the world point placed at frame center; camera.scale is zoom. Render transform: translate(960 - x*scale, 540 - y*scale) scale(scale), transform-origin top-left of the world.
camera_model.keyframe_format: {f: frame relative to scene start, x, y, scale, easing}
camera_model.depth: Optional parallax layers carry z in [-1000, 300]; layer offset = camera delta * (1 + z/1000).
camera_model.motion_blur: Use <CameraMotionBlur shutterAngle={180} samples={8}> only around moves faster than ~1.5 screen-widths per second; never on static or slow scenes (render cost multiplies by samples).

transition_language.reason: Assertion: a statement replaces the previous one without softening.
The camera keeps moving from type into fragments, so the gap feels spatial.
Fragmentation resolves into one thread, which becomes Navis.
The neutral line becomes Navis blue: the reveal.
We enter the agents' world through its label.
The product appears as a physical object in the dark world.
Time passes: fade to ink, hold 'DAY 2', fade up.
Cut on Enter: one terminal flows into the next question.
Isolation shown structurally: one window becomes three separate ones.
Crossing from agents to people through the shared line.
Continuous camera inside one product flow (no visible transition).
Cause -> effect: 'Reply sent' cuts to the message arriving in the recipient's inbox.
The people product is revealed as one half of a system.
The seam bends into the loop: the system's next step.
The loop collapses into the logomark.

demo_environment.principle: A fictional company with REAL accounts, REAL mail and REAL calendar events, so the product's pipeline runs for real on safe data.

people.name: Daniel Ortiz
people.role: customer contact who emailed about renewal terms (recipient in S14)

demo_environment.domains: Two demo domains Navis Labs controls (one for Fieldstone, one for the customer), with Google Workspace accounts for the people above. Never use personal or customer domains.
demo_environment.repository: fieldstone-api: a small demo service with a billing module, its own CLAUDE.md containing the line: 'At milestones, record state with `navis workstate checkpoint` (--decision, --open, --completed, --last-verified).' Never film inside the Devtool repo (its .claude/settings.local.json holds a real API key).
data_seeding: Author 15–25 realistic emails and 5–8 calendar events over two weeks between the demo accounts, including a pricing review meeting and Daniel's renewal question 3 days before filming.
Connect Google for Maya through the normal Navis AI onboarding and let ingestion and brief generation run naturally.
Never use POST /integrations/seed or any synthetic signal injection.
credential_hygiene: Keys live only in environment variables of the recording shells
No command that prints a key (`navis config show`, `env`, `cat .env`) is ever run on camera
Rotate all demo keys after the shoot

capture_defaults.machine: macOS, Do Not Disturb on, menu bar hidden or cropped, clean user account named 'demo'
capture_defaults.display: logical 1920x1080 HiDPI (3840x2160 physical) so the content captures at 2x
capture_defaults.recorder: any recorder that can hide the system cursor; 60 fps; ProRes 422 HQ (or HEVC ≥ 80 Mb/s)
capture_defaults.terminal: Geist Mono 15 pt, background #14130F, foreground #EDEBE6, prompt 'fieldstone-api %', window 1600x1000 logical
capture_defaults.browser: clean Chrome profile, no extensions, bookmarks bar hidden, 100% zoom, window 1600x1000 logical
capture_defaults.cursor: hidden in all recordings; operator moves deliberately so UI hover states are captured; synthetic cursor added in Remotion
capture_defaults.typing: operator types at a natural pace; may be ramped ≤2x in edit; never replaced with synthetic text
capture_defaults.waits: record the full real wait; compress only by cutting, and disclose via the legal line
capture_defaults.takes: minimum 3 clean takes per recording; keep raw files and a log of timestamps

remotion_architecture.timeline_strategy: Absolute timing. Each scene is a <Sequence from={start_frame} durationInFrames={duration_frames + out_overlap}>; transitions are implemented inside scenes from enter/exit progress over their overlap windows (frames listed in motion_system.transition_language). This preserves the absolute VO and music timings in this spec.
remotion_architecture.video_handling: <OffthreadVideo> with startFrom/endAt per recording segment; speed ramps via playbackRate only within the limits in recording_plan.capture_defaults; never time-remap a confirmation state.
remotion_architecture.audio_handling: VO lines placed with <Sequence from> at voiceover.timing; music ducking via a volume callback reading VO activity windows; master loudness verified after render.
guards: Throw at render time if endingVariant is 'B' or 'C' and approvals.json does not approve U03/U04
Throw if any scene with status 'future' renders without the 'NEXT' label
Lint: every onscreen_text id used by a scene exists in onscreen_copy.deck
remotion_architecture.performance: CameraMotionBlur only in T_ZOOM_THROUGH and the first frames of S06/S15; premount heavy video sequences; use proxies in studio.

quality_bar.standard: Every frame could appear in a keynote. If a frame needs explaining, it is cut.
checks: Each scene communicates one idea in under 2 seconds of viewing.
At most one line of film typography visible at once.
No UI frame shows more than one primary action in focus.
Product text on screen is legible at 1080p when the camera holds (≥14 px effective).
Cursor never moves without a destination; every pause has a reason.
A first-time viewer can say, after one watch, which product is for people and which is for agents.

claims_to_avoid: Any availability language: 'available now', 'install now', 'public API', 'production-ready', 'now live for everyone', 'npm install', 'pip install navis-sdk'
Any URL other than navislabs.in (no api.navislabs.in, mcp.navislabs.in, app.navis.ai, /developers, localhost, staging)
Automatic capture of decisions, files or tests into the work state
Agents learning from their own outcomes, 'self-improving', 'learns from every interaction' (present tense)
'Read-only' or 'never writes back' (Navis sends with approval)
Slack as a working integration; Notion, GitHub, Jira, HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoom; reading document contents (Drive is metadata only); meeting transcripts
Absolute security language ('never', 'impossible', 'unbreakable'), SOC 2, compliance certifications
Any metric, benchmark, customer count, signal count or ROI figure
'$70M raised', '$70M funding', '$70M round' (and '$70M valuation' unless U03 is approved)
Partnership or endorsement by Anthropic, Cursor or Google; their names are used only to describe compatibility
Team-shared work state, Claude-to-Codex/Cursor hand-off, agent work appearing inside Navis AI
Organizational intelligence as a present-tense metric ('intelligence score')
